↓
「データを見ると」に置き換え。

AI利用量を評価に入れたらそうなる。難しいが成果で評価すべき。日本もClaude CodeなどのAIエージェントが普及しきった1-2年後には同じ課題に直面しそう。

>

きっかけはtokenmaxxing。AI利用量を評価に組み込んだら、社員は不要なタスクまでAIに投げてトークンを稼ぎ始めた。Amazonは社内ランキングを廃止し、評価軸を「出荷コード」へ切り替えた。Uberは年間AI予算を4ヶ月で溶かし、1ツール月1500ドルの上限を引いた。

効くのは、ものさしの作り直しだ。Cognitionは「成果が出なければ最大1000万ドルを肩代わり」とまで踏み込んだ。何トークン燃やすかではなく、いくらの仕事をしたか。問われるのはそこだ。

AI活用の巧拙は、もう導入率では測れない。同じ予算でどれだけ価値を絞り出せるか。コスト管理力こそが、これからのAI活用力になるわけだ。

Google I/O 2026まとめ🇺🇸

Los Angeles、San Francisco、New Yorkと怒涛のアメリカ出張が終わった久々の土日なので、備忘録として。

ーー

2年連続で招待いただき、本当に光栄でした。

今年も世界中のトップクリエイターやインフルエンサーの方々と交流できて、かなり刺激を受けました。

東南アジア圏の登録者100万超えの方々とも話したのですが、中にはAI領域なのにXアカウントを持っていない方もいてびっくりしました。

でも、その分ショート動画はめちゃくちゃ強い。時代はショート動画なので、来年までに頑張ろうと思いました。

そして、今回は日本チームのメンバーも以前より増えて、みんなで行動する時間も多かったです。普段なかなかゆっくり話せない方々とも現地で色々話せて、知見も広がりましたし、普通にめちゃくちゃ楽しかったです。（有名人も多数でテンション上がりました！）

まさに大人の修学旅行みたいな時間でした。

そしてGoogleはやっぱりすごい。

モデルもプロダクトも数が多く、検索、Gemini、動画、開発、デバイス、エージェントまで、全方位でカバーしているのが本当に圧倒的でした。

正直、発表が多すぎて追うのはかなり大変でしたが、それだけ進化のスピードが異常だということ。

改めて、素晴らしい機会を準備いただいたGoogleの皆さまに心から感謝しています。

来年もまたこの場所に呼んでいただけるように、これからも全力で発信していきます🔥

いつも応援してくださるフォロワーの皆様も、本当にありがとうございます🙏

posts.content:
Claude Code users are split into two
groups right now.

Group 1 is prompting it like a smarter Copilot and getting smarter Copilot results.

Group 2 gave it a memory, a planning phase, dedicated MCPs for each stage of development, and pre-written prompts that make it think like a staff engineer before touching a single file.

Group 2 is lapping everyone and nobody's talking about it.

The difference isn't talent. It's not even prompt skill. It's that they stopped treating it as a tool and started treating it as a system.

Plan → Code → Review → Test → Document. Each phase has its own context, its own tools, its own prompt. Nothing bleeds together. Nothing gets lost.

That's what this setup is. CLAUDE.md as the brain. Memory MCP so decisions persist. Context7 so it always has fresh docs. GitHub MCP so it's actually reading your repo, not guessing.

And the prompts are already written. The whole thing is free and public.

The gap this creates compounds every single week. Some people reading this will use it. Most won't. That's kind of the point.

The person who BUILT Claude Code, Boris Cherny, and the engineer many call the Godfather of AI, Andrej Karpathy, just independently arrived at the same conclusion:

The future of software engineering
posts.content:
The person who BUILT Claude Code, Boris Cherny, and the engineer many call the Godfather of AI, Andrej Karpathy, just independently arrived at the same conclusion:

The future of software engineering isn't better prompts.

It's better systems.

I combined both of their CLAUDE.md files into a single framework, and the overlap is fascinating.

Despite coming from different backgrounds, both are obsessed with the same ideas:

→ Plan before coding
→ Verify everything
→ Keep solutions simple
→ Use AI agents in parallel
→ Learn from every mistake
→ Optimize for correctness, not speed

And that's the biggest signal.

The smartest people in AI are no longer talking about prompting.

They're talking about workflows.

Karpathy's philosophy is centered around disciplined execution:

• Plan Mode First
• Verify Relentlessly
• Surgical Edits Only
• Goal-Driven Execution
• Parallel AI Agents
• Simplicity Above Everything

Boris pushes it even further with self-improving systems:

• Every mistake becomes a lesson
• Every correction updates the system
• Every project compounds knowledge
• Agents continuously improve through feedback loops

His rule is simple:

«If the same mistake happens twice, the system failed.»

Karpathy's insight is equally powerful:

«Don't tell the model what to do. Tell it what success looks like.»

That single shift changes everything.

From:

"Write this function."

To:

"Here's the objective, constraints, tests, edge cases, and verification criteria. Iterate until correct."

That's not prompting.

That's management.

And that's exactly why CLAUDE.md files are exploding across the AI engineering world.

They're not prompts.

They're encoded engineering culture.

A persistent operating system for AI agents.

The most advanced teams today are already running multiple agents simultaneously:

• One researching
• One coding
• One debugging
• One writing tests
• One reviewing outputs
• One validating edge cases

Not AI-assisted coding.

AI orchestration.

The biggest opportunity over the next decade may not belong to the engineers who write the best code.

It may belong to the engineers who build the best systems around AI agents.

We're witnessing the shift from:

Prompt Engineering → Workflow Engineering

Single Agents → Agent Teams

Manual Execution → Autonomous Systems

And both Boris Cherny and Andrej Karpathy are pointing in exactly the same direction.

The future belongs to engineers who can orchestrate intelligence, not just use it.

posts.content: I researched human happiness for three years while working on my first book. One thing I learned was that happiness was really about attention. The happiest people didn't have perfect lives. But the imperfections were never their focus. They found joy in ordinary days. Gratitude in small moments. Meaning in simple things. Happiness is about attention, not perfection.
